concept.name: Effective spread
concept.definition: A measure of the execution cost actually paid, defined relative to the midpoint of the national best bid and offer at the time of order receipt: for buy orders, twice the difference between the execution price and the midpoint; for sell orders, twice the difference between the midpoint and the execution price (SEC Rule 600(b)(8)).
concept.intuition: It captures what a liquidity demander really paid against the pre-trade benchmark price, so price improvement inside the quotes shows up as a smaller spread.
concept.mechanics: Computed per execution using the NBBO midpoint at order receipt, then share-weighted across executions (average effective spread); dividing by the midpoint gives the percentage effective spread. It is a standard output of SEC Rule 605 execution-quality reports.
concept.formula: ES_buy = 2(P_exec - M); ES_sell = 2(M - P_exec), where M is the NBBO midpoint at the time of order receipt.
concept.failure_modes: The midpoint benchmark can be stale or misleading in fast markets and wide-spread stocks, and the measure depends on the order-receipt time convention. It also ignores the market impact of large orders that walk the book and the opportunity cost of unfilled orders.
concept.misconceptions: A low effective spread does not mean trading was free; it excludes commissions, fees, delay costs, and impact beyond the first execution.
concept.example: NBBO midpoint is $100.01 at order receipt; a buy executes at $100.02, giving an effective spread of $0.02, equal to the quoted spread; execution at $100.01 gives $0.00.

citations.source: 17 CFR 242.600 - NMS security designation and definitions (Regulation NMS Rule 600)
